{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-ks-c","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"c195b2cf287b8deddf8bb06c79377ed2fd4b69a7892f53a1739864ba96f9f7a2","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-ks-class-c:lineage:50","source_registry_sha256":"c7fb2073a9e8bb6a73d0151458fe04991b703d84f882b00a01bedfcea433c383","source_liveness_sha256":"94328be42cc10cf86af8e486b41bc40c72c45e4700d27b9b46d1f3d2feac7bb6"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Driver-license test preparation","heading":"C2 — Driver-license test preparation","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Driver-license test preparation

FACT_ID: sec11-R01 | anchor: A100
The basic-control test may occur off the street, on the road-test route or in both settings. [A100]
Source: [A100 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec11-R02 | anchor: A100
The basic-control test includes at least two exercises from forward and reverse two-point turns, a three-point turn and left- or right-side parallel parking. [A100]
Source: [A100 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec11-R03 | anchor: A100
The handbook recommends practicing basic-control exercises in safe areas with a properly licensed parent, guardian or friend older than 21. [A100]
Source: [A100 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec11-R04 | anchor: A100
The examiner explains each exercise and allows questions before its completion. [A100]
Source: [A100 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec11-R05 | anchor: A100
A basic-control reversal is a stop followed by a direction change to improve position; stopping without changing direction does not count. [A100]
Source: [A100 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec11-R06 | anchor: A100
Each direction reversal in a basic-control exercise is scored as an error. [A100]
Source: [A100 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec11-R07 | anchor: A100
Touching or crossing an exercise line or cone with the vehicle counts as an encroachment except for mirror contact. [A100]
Source: [A100 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec11-R08 | anchor: A100
Each basic-control encroachment is scored as an error. [A100]
Source: [A100 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec11-R09 | anchor: A100
Use the correct signal while turning or backing in an exercise; omitted or incorrect signals count as errors, and an auto-canceled signal may need reactivation. [A100]
Source: [A100 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec11-R10 | anchor: A100
Check traffic before entering or leaving a roadway during an exercise and ensure both directions are clear; omitted head checks affect scoring. [A100]
Source: [A100 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec11-R11 | anchor: A100
Finish the exercise in the position the examiner specifies; an incorrect final position adds points. [A100]
Source: [A100 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec11-R12 | anchor: A101
In the forward two-point exercise, enter a driveway, alley or marked space until the rear clears the front cones and the vehicle is outside the road. [A101]
Source: [A101 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec11-R13 | anchor: A101
The forward two-point exercise then backs right into the street and drives forward to return toward the starting area. [A101]
Source: [A101 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec11-R14 | anchor: A101
The reverse two-point exercise starts by passing the entrance and backing right until the front clears the front cones and the vehicle is outside the road. [A101]
Source: [A101 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec11-R15 | anchor: A101
After the reverse two-point setup, drive left into the street toward the starting area and continue out of the exercise. [A101]
Source: [A101 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec11-R16 | anchor: A102
The three-point exercise may use a real road or a cone-and-line area to demonstrate reversal on a two-lane road. [A102]
Source: [A102 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec11-R17 | anchor: A102
For right-side parallel parking, pass the space, back into it completely and finish within 12 inches of the curb side without crossing side or rear boundaries. [A102]
Source: [A102 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec11-R18 | anchor: A102
For left-side parallel parking, pass the space and back fully into it within 12 inches of the curb side while respecting side and rear boundaries. [A102]
Source: [A102 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec11-R19 | anchor: A104
The road test follows an examiner-directed route covering varied traffic situations and evaluates maneuvers and general driving behavior. [A104]
Source: [A104 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec11-R20 | anchor: A104
The handbook recommends starting road practice in low-traffic residential areas with a properly licensed adult older than 21 before progressing to more complex traffic. [A104]
Source: [A104 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec11-R21 | anchor: A104
For a tested turn, check traffic, signal correctly, brake smoothly and enter the appropriate turning lane safely. [A104]
Source: [A104 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec11-R22 | anchor: A104
If a stop is needed before a turn, stop smoothly behind the applicable line, crosswalk or sign, with the front wheels straight. [A104]
Source: [A104 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec11-R23 | anchor: A104
The road-test guidance uses visibility of the preceding vehicle's rear tires as a stopping-gap cue. [A104]
Source: [A104 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec11-R24 | anchor: A104
During a tested turn, search all directions, keep both hands steering, accelerate smoothly and yield to other traffic and pedestrians. [A104]
Source: [A104 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec11-R25 | anchor: A104
Keep the turn within the proper lane without entering opposing traffic or running over the curb. [A104]
Source: [A104 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec11-R26 | anchor: A104
After a turn, confirm the proper exit lane and canceled signal; before a needed move right, signal and check mirrors and blind spots, then move only when safe. [A104]
Source: [A104 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec11-R27 | anchor: A104
On intersection approach during the test, check traffic all around, brake smoothly and hold lane position. [A104]
Source: [A104 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec11-R28 | anchor: A104
When passing through an intersection during the test, slow as needed, yield to users inside it and avoid changing lanes. [A104]
Source: [A104 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec11-R29 | anchor: A104
After clearing an intersection, continue checking behind and accelerate smoothly; a needed lane change requires a signal and mirror and blind-spot checks. [A104]
Source: [A104 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec11-R30 | anchor: A105
For urban and rural portions of the test, maintain traffic checks, safe following room and correct lane position while keeping pace without exceeding the posted limit. [A105]
Source: [A105 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0105]

FACT_ID: sec11-R31 | anchor: A105
The road test may request a left lane change and then a return right; use mirrors, shoulder checks, signals and smooth safe movement, then cancel the signal. [A105]
Source: [A105 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0105]

FACT_ID: sec11-R32 | anchor: A105
Before an expressway test merge, check mirrors and the target-side blind spot, signal and accelerate smoothly into the proper lane without crossing solid lines. [A105]
Source: [A105 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0105]

FACT_ID: sec11-R33 | anchor: A105
After an expressway merge, cancel the signal and maintain appropriate lane position, spacing and speed with continuing traffic checks. [A105]
Source: [A105 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0105]

FACT_ID: sec11-R34 | anchor: A105
For the expressway exit, check traffic and signal, then brake within the deceleration lane while maintaining its boundaries, posted warning speeds and space. [A105]
Source: [A105 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0105]

FACT_ID: sec11-R35 | anchor: A105
For limited-access entry, mirror and head checks and a signal precede a smooth merge or turn; avoid stopping unless necessary and do not cross solid lines. [A105]
Source: [A105 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0105]

FACT_ID: sec11-R36 | anchor: A105
On a limited-access road, maintain correct lane position, speed and spacing while scanning all directions. [A105]
Source: [A105 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0105]

FACT_ID: sec11-R37 | anchor: A105
For a limited-access exit, check and signal, slow smoothly in the deceleration or turning lane, obey warning speeds, preserve spacing and cancel the signal after leaving. [A105]
Source: [A105 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0105]

FACT_ID: sec11-R38 | anchor: A106
For a curve on the road test, check traffic and reduce speed before entry, remain in the lane and follow warning signs at a safe curve speed. [A106]
Source: [A106 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec11-R39 | anchor: A106
The road-test examiner may ask the applicant to identify a sign just passed at any point on the route. [A106]
Source: [A106 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0106]

Misconceptions: The knowledge exam is untimed despite an estimated completion duration; four attempts are not unlimited retakes; stopping without reversing is not a reversal error; practical-test failures are distinct from knowledge-test scoring.
Mnemonics: Editorial cue: eligibility, equipment, instructions, observations, finish. It organizes preparation without supplying an official scoring formula.
Glossary: Distinguish knowledge test, pre-trip inspection, reversal, encroachment, final position and automatic road-test failure using the sourced blocks.
Dynamic facts: Test access, retake policy, required documents and examiner procedures are edition-bound. Currentness and image-specific geometry remain debt. No sample-question text, live question-bank membership or practical-test service is asserted.

FACT_ID: sec11-R40 | anchor: A106
Use steady, smooth brake pressure rather than harsh braking during ordinary test maneuvers. [A106]
Source: [A106 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec11-R41 | anchor: A106
Keep both hands on the wheel's outside unless operating another control, and return the hand after using it. [A106]
Source: [A106 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec11-R42 | anchor: A106
The test's steering guidance accepts hand-over-hand or hand-to-hand methods with the hands outside the rim. [A106]
Source: [A106 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec11-R43 | anchor: A106
Keep off curbs and sidewalks and avoid intersection lane changes during the test. [A106]
Source: [A106 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec11-R44 | anchor: A106
Check traffic and mirrors before, during and after intersections, turns and lane changes, adding head checks when needed for merging or changing lanes. [A106]
Source: [A106 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec11-R45 | anchor: A106
Use timely required turn signals and cancel them after the maneuver. [A106]
Source: [A106 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec11-R46 | anchor: A106
For a stop sign or stop signal, remain behind the marked line, crosswalk or sidewalk instead of stopping in the intersection. [A106]
Source: [A106 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec11-R47 | anchor: A107
Not using a seat belt is an automatic road-test failure. [A107]
Source: [A107 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec11-R48 | anchor: A107
Failing to check blind spots is an automatic road-test failure. [A107]
Source: [A107 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec11-R49 | anchor: A107
A moving citation, ignored signs or signals, speeding, rolling stops or other traffic-law disobedience causes automatic road-test failure. [A107]
Source: [A107 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec11-R50 | anchor: A107
Failure to yield to pedestrians or other road users causes automatic road-test failure. [A107]
Source: [A107 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec11-R51 | anchor: A107
An avoidable crash or physical contact with another vehicle, object or pedestrian causes automatic road-test failure. [A107]
Source: [A107 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec11-R52 | anchor: A107
An unsafe act or forcing another driver to evade a collision causes automatic road-test failure. [A107]
Source: [A107 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec11-R53 | anchor: A107
Unnecessary travel over a curb or sidewalk causes automatic road-test failure. [A107]
Source: [A107 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec11-R54 | anchor: A107
Examiner intervention to control the vehicle causes automatic road-test failure. [A107]
Source: [A107 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec11-R55 | anchor: A107
The road test includes basic-control exercises in real traffic settings with examiner instructions, after which route driving resumes. [A107]
Source: [A107 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec11-R56 | anchor: A107
At the end, the examiner discusses each test's result and suggestions for improvement. [A107]
Source: [A107 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0107]
